Features.label: Features
Features.h2: Built for <accent>video creators</accent> who care about accuracy.
Features.intro: A video-to-text converter transcribes the spoken audio inside a video into written text. Modern AI speech models identify words, separate speakers, and attach timestamps — producing an editable transcript in minutes instead of hours. Scribix runs the same class of speech model that powers professional transcription suites — sign in with Google to get started and produce output clean enough to publish.

items.title: Speaker recognition, up to 8 voices
items.body: Voice-fingerprinting separates and labels each turn — Speaker 1, Speaker 2 become real names with one click. Perfect for interviews, podcasts, and panels.

items.title: 200+ languages, auto-detected
items.body: From Mandarin to Maltese with code-switching support. The model adapts mid-recording when speakers swap languages.

items.title: Word-level timestamps
items.body: Click any word to play that exact moment. Timestamps export with SRT and VTT subtitles ready for video players.

items.title: Five export formats
items.body: TXT, DOCX, SRT, VTT, and CSV — covers documents, captions, spreadsheets, and review workflows without extra conversion.

items.title: Studio-grade accuracy
items.body: 99.9% on clear audio in primary languages, measured on a 50-hour benchmark of TED talks, podcasts, and interviews. Background noise and accents handled gracefully.

items.title: Files deleted in 24 hours
items.body: TLS 1.3 in transit, AES-256 at rest, processing in encrypted memory. SOC 2-aligned, GDPR-compliant. We never train models on your audio.

HowItWorks.label: How it works
HowItWorks.h2Part2: <accent>Video to text in under a minute.</accent>

steps.title: Upload your video or audio file.
steps.body: Drag and drop an MP4, MOV, AVI, MKV, WebM, MP3, WAV, or M4A file up to 1 GB. No format conversion needed — Scribix handles every common media container.

steps.title: AI transcribes with speaker labels.
steps.body: Our model auto-detects the language (200+ supported), separates up to 8 speakers, and attaches timestamps to every word. A 1-hour video transcribes in about 90 seconds.

steps.title: Edit, copy, or export.
steps.body: Click any word to play that exact moment. Edit inline, then download as TXT, DOCX, SRT, VTT, or CSV — or copy the full transcript into your editor.

UseCases.label: Use Cases
UseCases.intro: From creators repurposing 90 minutes of footage into shorts, to journalists quoting 2-hour interviews accurately — video-to-text is how recorded conversation becomes published work. Scribix is the workhorse behind it.

items.title: Video creators
items.body: Generate captions for accessibility, repurpose long videos into blog posts, build searchable episode archives. Word-level timestamps make it trivial to extract viral clips with [12:04 – 12:38] precision.

items.title: Podcasters & Producers
items.body: Convert each episode into show notes, blog content, and SEO-indexed transcripts — the difference between getting found on Google and not. Speaker labels arrive ready to publish.

items.title: Journalists & Interviewers
items.body: Transcribe a 90-minute interview while you walk to the next one. Speaker labels mean you can quote sources accurately without re-listening — quote-ready text in a fraction of the time.

items.title: Researchers & UX
items.body: Run qualitative coding on focus groups, lectures, and field recordings without paying $1.50/min for human transcription. Tag themes, search every word, export to Dovetail or Notion.

items.title: Students
items.body: Turn a 2-hour lecture into searchable notes. Mark a confusing moment, click the word, hear it again. Try it free, then a single Starter month covers an entire semester of lectures.

items.title: Legal & Compliance
items.body: First-pass transcripts of depositions, board meetings, and compliance interviews — then have a human verify the parts that matter. Time-coded transcripts and an auditable processing chain. SOC 2-aligned.

Comparison.h2: Faster, more accurate, <accent>and a real free trial.</accent>

faqs.question: Can I start for free?
faqs.answer: Yes. Free includes 45 lifetime minutes so you can test transcript quality before choosing a paid plan.

faqs.question: What counts as transcription minutes?
faqs.answer: Minutes are based on the length of the audio or video you transcribe. A 30-minute file uses 30 transcription minutes.

faqs.question: Do unused minutes roll over?
faqs.answer: Monthly plan minutes reset each billing cycle. Annual plans are intended to provide the full annual allowance upfront at renewal.

faqs.question: What is the max file length?
faqs.answer: Free supports files up to 45 minutes, Starter supports files up to 1 hour, and Pro supports files up to 10 hours.

faqs.question: Can I change plans later?
faqs.answer: Yes. The plan structure is designed so you can start on Starter and move to Pro when longer files, priority queue, or AI outputs become important.

faqs.question: Is there a free trial on paid plans?
faqs.answer: Yes. Starter and Pro Unlimited both include 14 days free, and you can cancel anytime before the trial ends.

FAQ.contactPrefix: Can't find what you're looking for? Email

items.q: Is Scribix really free for video to text?
items.a: Yes. The free trial only needs a Google sign-in — no credit card. You get 45 minutes of transcription to try the quality before you decide. Paid plans unlock longer files, priority queue, team libraries, and longer file retention.

items.q: What video formats does Scribix support?
items.a: MP4, MOV, AVI, MKV, and WebM up to 1 GB each. Audio-only files (MP3, WAV, M4A) are also supported.

items.q: How accurate is Scribix's video-to-text?
items.a: 99.9% on clear audio in primary languages, measured against a 50-hour benchmark of TED talks, podcasts, and interviews. Accuracy drops slightly with heavy accents, background music, or low-bitrate audio — but speaker labels and word-level timestamps make corrections quick.

items.q: How many languages does Scribix support?
items.a: 200+, with automatic language detection. The model handles code-switching (English ↔ Spanish, English ↔ Mandarin) within the same recording. No need to pre-select a primary language.

items.q: Can Scribix tell different speakers apart?
items.a: Yes. Voice-fingerprinting identifies up to 8 distinct speakers and labels every line accordingly. You can rename Speaker 1, Speaker 2, etc. to actual names after transcription, and the model remembers voices across recordings.

items.q: How long does video-to-text transcription take?
items.a: Around 1 minute of compute time per hour of video for clear-audio MP4s. A 30-minute meeting takes about 45 seconds.

items.q: Is my data secure when I upload a video?
items.a: Files are uploaded over TLS 1.3, processed in encrypted memory, and deleted within 24 hours. We don't train models on user audio. SOC 2-aligned infrastructure, GDPR-compliant data handling, and EU + US regional processing options.

items.q: What can I export the transcript as?
items.a: Five formats: TXT (plain), DOCX (Word), SRT (subtitles), VTT (web subtitles), and CSV (spreadsheet-friendly). Click-to-edit inline before exporting.

items.q: Does Scribix work for podcasts and audio-only files?
items.a: Yes — but for an audio-first workflow, our dedicated audio-to-text tool is purpose-built for that intent. Same engine, same accuracy, audio-tuned UI.

items.a: Yes. Scribix requests speaker labels during transcription, so conversations can be separated by speaker when the recording quality supports it.

items.q: How many languages does Scribix support?
items.a: Scribix supports transcription in 200+ languages with automatic language detection.

items.q: How accurate is MP3 transcription?
items.a: Scribix can reach 99.9% accuracy on clear audio, but accuracy depends on audio quality, accents, noise, overlapping speakers, and specialized vocabulary. Review important transcripts before publishing or relying on them.

items.q: Does MP3 compression affect transcription quality?
items.a: It can. Clear spoken MP3 files usually transcribe well, but very low-bitrate audio, loud background noise, music, or muffled voices can reduce accuracy.

items.q: Is my MP3 stored forever?
items.a: No. Scribix's privacy policy says uploaded audio and video files are deleted automatically after 7 days. Transcripts stay in your account until you delete them or close your account.

items.q: Do I need an account to convert MP3 to text?
items.a: Yes. Scribix requires Google sign-in before upload so your transcripts can be saved to your library and managed from your dashboard.

faq.intro: Caption availability, exports, privacy, and paid summaries are explained plainly before you paste a YouTube URL.

items.q: How do I turn a YouTube video into a transcript?
items.a: Paste the YouTube URL into Scribix, check the available caption tracks, choose a language, and import the transcript. Scribix saves the transcript to your account so you can review, copy, export, or summarize it on a paid plan.

items.q: Does Scribix work with every YouTube video?
items.a: No. The YouTube URL workflow works when Scribix can access at least one caption track for the video. If the video has no captions, is private, restricted, deleted, or blocked, Scribix may not be able to import a transcript.

items.q: Does Scribix download the YouTube video or audio?
items.a: No. Scribix imports available YouTube captions. It does not download the YouTube video or audio for this workflow.

items.q: Can Scribix generate a transcript if a YouTube video has no captions?
items.a: Not from the YouTube URL alone. If you own the media file, use Scribix's video-to-text or audio-to-text upload flow to generate a new AI transcript from the file.

items.q: Is YouTube to transcript free in Scribix?
items.a: Yes. Scribix includes 10 YouTube caption imports per day on the free plan with Google sign-in and no credit card.

items.q: What can I export the YouTube transcript as?
items.a: Scribix can export completed transcripts as TXT, DOCX, SRT, VTT, or CSV. You can also copy transcript text directly from the app.

items.q: Can I choose the transcript language?
items.a: Yes, when the YouTube video has multiple caption tracks. Scribix shows the available caption languages and lets you choose which one to import.

items.q: Can I summarize a YouTube transcript?
items.a: Yes. Paid users can use AI summaries after importing the YouTube transcript into Scribix.

items.q: Are imported YouTube transcripts accurate?
items.a: They are as accurate as the selected YouTube caption track. Manual captions are usually stronger than auto-generated captions, but every transcript should be reviewed before quoting, publishing, or using it for high-stakes decisions.
